cover.title: Your Salary Isn't In Your Score
cover.label: INCOME

lines.text: Your salary isn't in your credit score. At all.
lines.say: Your salary isn't in your credit score. At all.

lines.text: Credit reports don't list income, and FICO only uses your report.
lines.say: Credit reports don't list income, and FICO only uses your report.
FICO weighs payment history most: thirty-five percent.

lines.text: Amounts owed, 30%. Then history length, 15%, and new credit plus mix, 20%.
lines.say: Amounts owed, thirty percent. Then history length, fifteen percent, and new credit plus mix, twenty percent.

lines.text: Earn $200,000 and pay late? You can score lower than someone earning $40,000 who always pays on time.
lines.say: Earn two hundred thousand dollars and pay late? You can score lower than someone earning forty thousand who always pays on time.

lines.text: One late payment of 30-plus days can stay on your report up to 7 years.
lines.say: One late payment of thirty-plus days can stay on your report up to seven years.

scene.label: How long a late payment can stay

lines.text: Big balances hurt too. $5,000 owed on a $10,000 limit means 50% utilization.
lines.say: Big balances hurt too. Five thousand dollars owed on a ten thousand dollar limit means fifty percent utilization.

lines.text: Pay it down to $1,000, and it's 10%. Lower usually scores better.
lines.say: Pay it down to a thousand, and it's ten percent. Lower usually scores better.

lines.text: The average FICO score peaked at 718 in 2023. By spring 2026, it was 714.
lines.say: The average FICO score peaked at seven eighteen in twenty twenty-three. By spring twenty twenty-six, it was seven fourteen.

lines.text: Lenders check income separately. The score is about how you handle debt.

post.title: Your salary isn't in your credit score. Here's what is.
post.ig:
Your salary isn't in your credit score. At all.
Credit reports don't include income, and FICO scores use only what's in your report.
FICO weights: payment history 35%, amounts owed 30%, history length 15%, new credit and mix 20%.
Example: $5,000 owed on a $10,000 limit = 50% utilization; $1,000 owed = 10%.
A late payment can stay on your report up to 7 years.
Sources: myFICO; CFPB; FICO (average score 714, spring 2026).
News and education, not financial advice.
